speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the color and consistency of your urine, and do you notice any blood or cloudiness? Also, has the fever persisted or worsened since your recent sinusitis treatment?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your urine become dark or bloody, and do you experience pain or burning when you urinate? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, and Cytospin Stained With Hansel's Solution revealing 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Vital signs indicate Temperature 37.9°C (100.2°F), Blood Pressure 145/90 mmHg, Heart Rate 75 bpm, and Respiratory Rate 16 breaths/min. General Examination reveals Mild flank tenderness with no rebound or guarding, and Renal Angles show Mild tenderness on percussion. Serum Biochemistry indicates Elevated Urea and Elevated Creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any rash, hives, or swelling in your face or hands recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Exam.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis secondary to amoxicillin/cephalexin exposure. The combination of fever, flank pain, sterile pyuria, and eosinophiluria following antibiotic use is classic for this condition.
